title: How do we split these decimals into parts?
description: Four decimals are written as sums of tenths, hundredths and thousandths by reading each digit with its place. A last step adds the parts of one decimal back.
teaching_notes: One idea: each digit after the point is a count of its own place, and a unit can be written as hundredths. Watch for children who leave out the unit in one point zero two.

source: Figure it Out (end of chapter), Q2
video_script.why: The child has written parts of a unit as decimals and now goes the other way, from a decimal to its parts.
video_script.substitution: Each digit is read with its own place name, and a unit can be written as hundredths.
video_script.anchor: four decimals to be split into tenths, hundredths and thousandths
video_script.payoff_line: Read each digit with its own place name

final_answer.spoken: three tenths plus four hundredths; one unit plus two hundredths; eight tenths; three tenths plus six hundredths plus two thousandths

video_script.fraction_reading: tenths, hundredths and thousandths are said as words
video_script.design: The four decimals stay in the anchor band; each is split by place in the working band, and a last step adds the parts of 0.362 back.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; four decimals (a) 0.34 (b) 1.02 (c) 0.8 (d) 0.362; a question mark in the anchor band
narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about splitting decimals by place.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Four decimals are given, and each is to be written as a sum of parts.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Write each decimal as a sum of tenths, hundredths and thousandths.

beats.on_screen: the decimals stay on the board; Keeko sits beside them as the child
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a place value chart: units, a point, tenths, hundredths and thousandths; one unit bar cut into 100 hundredths

marks.chart: the chart of places is drawn
marks.digit: each digit is shown as a count of its place
marks.unit: a unit bar is shown as 100 hundredths

narration: <bookmark mark='chart'/>Here is the place value chart, with tenths, hundredths and thousandths after the point.
<bookmark mark='digit'/>Each digit after the point is a count of the parts in its own place.
<bookmark mark='unit'/>One whole unit can also be written as one hundred hundredths.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, zero point three four and one point zero two.
Also zero point eight and zero point three six two.

beats.on_screen: To find: each decimal as a sum of tenths, hundredths and thousandths
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each decimal as a sum of tenths, hundredths and thousandths.

marks.a: 0.34 is read as 3 tenths and 4 hundredths
marks.b: 1.02 is read as 1 unit, no tenths, 2 hundredths

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step one, zero point three four has three tenths and four hundredths.
<bookmark mark='aw'/>We write it as three tenths plus four hundredths.
<bookmark mark='b'/>One point zero two has one unit, no tenths and two hundredths.
<bookmark mark='bw'/>One unit is one hundred hundredths, so the sum is one hundred hundredths plus two hundredths.

marks.c: 0.8 is read as 8 tenths and 8/10 is written
marks.d: 0.362 is read as 3 tenths, 6 hundredths and 2 thousandths

narration: <bookmark mark='c'/>Step two, zero point eight has only eight tenths, so it is eight over ten.
<bookmark mark='d'/>Zero point three six two has three tenths, six hundredths and two thousandths.
<bookmark mark='dw'/>We write it as three over ten, six over a hundred and two over a thousand.

marks.chk: each part is changed to thousandths

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step three, put the answer back by adding the parts of the last decimal.
Those parts make three hundred sixty-two thousandths.
<bookmark mark='same'/>That is zero point three six two again.

marks.first: the first two answers are marked
marks.last: the last two answers are marked

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Read each digit with its own place name.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The first two are three tenths plus four hundredths, and one plus two hundredths.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last two are eight tenths, and three tenths plus six hundredths plus two thousandths.
